```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("R/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
health_small <- simulate_bdat602(n = 10000, seed = 602)
```

## Task 1 — Prepare data and distance matrix

```{r task1}
library(dplyr)

set.seed(602)
hc_sub <- health_small |>
  slice_sample(n = 500) |>
  select(age, bmi, num_claims) |>
  mutate(bmi = if_else(is.na(bmi), median(bmi, na.rm = TRUE), bmi)) |>
  na.omit()

hc_scaled <- scale(hc_sub)
dist_mat  <- dist(hc_scaled, method = "euclidean")

cat("Matrix dimensions:", nrow(as.matrix(dist_mat)), "×",
    ncol(as.matrix(dist_mat)), "\n")
```

## Task 2 — Fit hierarchical clustering and plot dendrogram

```{r task2}
hc_ward <- hclust(dist_mat, method = "ward.D2")

plot(hc_ward, labels = FALSE, hang = -1,
     main = "Dendrogram: Ward.D2 Linkage",
     xlab = "", ylab = "Height")
abline(h = 6, col = "red", lty = 2)
```

The dendrogram shows the merge hierarchy. The red line at height 6 suggests roughly 3–4 natural clusters.

## Task 3 — Cut at k = 3

```{r task3}
clusters <- cutree(hc_ward, k = 3)
table(clusters)
```

With Ward.D2 and k = 3, the clusters are typically balanced, each containing roughly 100–200 of the 500 sampled observations.
